requirement: Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. A file-range or Rust-item input MUST show its resolved file and inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its glob and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each subsection MUST show the exact recorded text in a fenced code block. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the implementation covers every obligation in `requirements.index.detail_format`, and the tests cover the main cases. One small marking gap remains (see the end). **Implementation, checked against each obligation** - **State badge:** `render_detail_sections` (src/index.rs) calls `shield_badge("evidence", state.label(), state.color())`. That function (src/lib.rs) builds an `https://img.shields.io/badge/...` static badge ``. Its alt text is "evidence ", for example "evidence Valid". - **Body as block quote labeled by kind:** the function writes a `## Requirement` or `## Example` heading, chosen from `DefinitionKind`. It then prefixes every line of the current definition text with `> `. The tests assert `## Requirement\n\n> Ready MUST work.\n> \n> ## Example` and `## Example\n\n> Pending case.`. They also assert that stale recorded text is not shown. - **Rationale and FIXME:** the rationale is pushed as raw Markdown under `## Rationale`. If it is empty, the page says "No rationale recorded." When `fixme_entries` is non-empty, a `## FIXME references` section lists the strings, HTML-escaped. `Judgment::fixme_entries` and `LoadedDetailEvidence::fixme_entries`/`borrowed` carry those strings through. - **Per-input subsection:** `render_input` emits `

Input N: …

`. The label names the selector: - `file range file:start–end` - `Rust item file selector` - `requirements glob …` - `definition …` - **Resolved location:** the same function calls `selector.resolve` (or uses the range directly for file ranges) and `render_source_location`. That prints `file:start–end` inclusively, for each matched definition. For a requirements glob the `SourceRange.name` field adds the definition's full name. Unresolved selectors are reported instead of being hidden. - **Exact text in a fenced code block:** `push_code_block` uses a fence longer than any backtick run in the text. It does not alter the text. If the input has no text array, it falls back to raw JSON. - **Highlighting:** `code_language` returns `rust,noplayground` for `.rs`, and `markdown`, `json`, `java`, `javascript`, `typescript` and `python` for the matching extensions. TOML uses `ini`, which the requirement allows. Requirements and definition inputs are fenced as `markdown`. **Tests** - `detail_page_renders_markdown_and_highlighted_input_sections` covers the badge, the block quote, the Rationale section, the input heading with its range, Rust highlighting, longer fences, and `.toml` rendered as `ini`. - `common_input_extensions_select_highlighting_languages` covers every language mapping. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` covers the badge and the quote in a built book. - `index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages` covers the Example label, "No rationale recorded." and the validation findings. - `valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` (tests/outcomes.rs) covers the FIXME badge and the FIXME references section. - tests/commands.rs checks the Rust-item and requirements-glob labels and line ranges through the shared renderer behind `info`. The book-page tests only exercise file-range inputs directly. **Minor observations (not blocking)** - `shield_badge` and `escape_html` in src/lib.rs are shared helpers marked for other requirements, not `detail_format`. - `InputSelector::resolve` is marked for the `ci.*` and `definitions.*` requirements. - The detail-specific behavior of these helpers is marked at their call sites. I consider that acceptable.
